title: Why CI is always on a detached HEAD, and what to do about it
summary: Your build script calls `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` and gets 'HEAD'. Understand why every CI system checks out a commit rather than a branch, and get the information you actually need.
mental_model: CI checks out an exact commit so the build is reproducible — a branch could move mid-run. That means there is no current branch, and any script that assumes one gets the literal string 'HEAD'.

write.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Naive version stamping — breaks on a detached HEAD.
branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
echo "building branch=$branch sha=$sha"

setup.run: git commit -q -m "Add app and CI stamp script"

steps.title: It works on your machine
steps.why: On a developer checkout there is a current branch, so the script prints something sensible. That is exactly why the bug reaches CI unnoticed.

steps.title: Simulate what CI does
steps.why: A CI runner clones and checks out the exact commit, not the branch — so the build cannot change underneath itself if someone pushes mid-run. `--detach` is precisely what `actions/checkout` and its equivalents do.

actions.run: sh -c 'git fetch -q origin feature/dosing && git checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD'

steps.expect: branch=HEAD — the literal string, which then ends up in an image tag.

verify.label: the CI workspace is on a detached HEAD

steps.title: Ask which branches contain this commit
steps.why: `branch -r --contains HEAD` answers 'where does this commit live'. It is the git-native way to recover the branch name, and it works even when no CI variable is available.
commands: sh -c 'git branch -r --contains HEAD | head -1 | sed "s|.*origin/||" | tr -d " "'
steps.expect: origin/feature/dosing — the branch, recovered from the commit.

verify.label: the branch name is recoverable from the commit

steps.title: Fix the stamp script
steps.why: Prefer the CI platform's variable when present, fall back to git, and never emit the literal 'HEAD'. Three lines, and the script now works identically on a laptop and on a runner.

write.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Robust on a detached HEAD and on a normal checkout.

branch="${CI_BRANCH:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}}"

if [ -z "$branch" ]; then
  branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
fi

if [ "$branch" = "HEAD" ]; then
  branch=$(git branch -r --contains HEAD 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's|.*origin/||' | tr -d ' ')
fi

[ -n "$branch" ] || branch="detached"

sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo "$sha")

echo "building branch=$branch sha=$sha version=$version"

steps.expect: A real branch name, a sha, and a version — on a detached HEAD.

verify.label: the script recovers the branch on a detached HEAD
verify.hint: fall back to git branch -r --contains HEAD

verify.label: …and never emits the literal string HEAD

steps.title: Check the version stamp too
steps.why: `git describe` needs tags, and a CI clone often has none. `--always` falls back to a sha instead of failing the build, and fetching tags makes the real version available.
steps.expect: A bare sha before fetching tags, then a proper v1.0.0-based version afterwards.

verify.label: the version stamp works once tags are fetched
verify.hint: git fetch --tags — CI clones do not always include them

steps.title: Prove the environment variable path works too
steps.why: When the platform supplies the branch, use it — it is authoritative and free. The git fallback exists for local runs and for platforms that do not.

steps.title: Commit the fix back
steps.why: The fix belongs in the repository, not in a runner's YAML. Copy it back to the working checkout and commit it so every future build has it.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "ci: make version stamping work on a detached HEAD"

verify.label: the fixed script works on a normal checkout as well
the stamp script works on an attached checkout
verify.hint: prefer the CI variable, fall back to git, never emit 'HEAD'

verify.label: the version comes from the tag once tags are fetched
the CI workspace is still detached — the fix is in the script, not the checkout

pitfalls: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns the literal string 'HEAD' when detached. Image tags called `HEAD` in a registry are always this bug.
`git branch --contains` needs the remote refs. A `--depth 1` clone of a single ref has none, so fetch the branch or use the platform variable.
`git describe` fails outright with no tags. Always pass `--always` in a build script, and fetch tags if you want real versions.
On a pull-request build, many platforms check out a temporary merge commit rather than your branch tip. `git log -1` there shows a commit nobody wrote.
Detached HEAD in CI is correct and deliberate. The fix is always in your script, never in forcing the runner onto a branch.
cheatsheet: which remote branches hold this commit
a human-readable name for any commit
a version string that never fails
